agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration, with UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory, Rocket Lab and Blue Origin
payload: Two spacecraft, Blue and Gold: 209 kg dry, 535 kg fuelled each
credit: Source: NASA. Twin spacecraft Blue and Gold from Rocket Lab; principal investigator Robert Lillis, UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory; launched by Blue Origin on New Glenn NG-2, 13 November 2025. Figures from NASA's press kit, launch blog and Earth-flyby release.

links.l: Liftoff: NASA's ESCAPADE begins journey to Mars (NASA blog)
NASA's ESCAPADE completes powered Earth flybys, now en route to Mars (NASA)

launch.source: NASA ESCAPADE press kit: 535 kg fuelled per spacecraft, two spacecraft. No C3 is published in the sources used

cruise.source: NASA ESCAPADE press kit and Earth-flyby release: about one year looping around Sun-Earth L2, then powered Earth flybys. The mapped arc is a schematic Earth-to-Mars transfer ellipse, not the loiter-and-flyby path

arrival.source: NASA ESCAPADE Earth-flyby release and press kit: orbit-insertion burns of about 11 minutes at 450 km into a 60-hour capture orbit

events.label: Launch — New Glenn NG-2
events.description: Launch Complex 36, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, 13 November 2025 at 3:55 pm EST (20:55 UTC). The booster, GS1 "Never Tell Me the Odds", landed on the landing platform vessel Jacklyn about nine minutes after liftoff.

events.label: Spacecraft separation
events.description: Blue and Gold separate from the New Glenn upper stage about 33.5 minutes after liftoff.

events.label: Earth flyby — Blue
events.description: Blue's powered Earth flyby on 7 November 2026, after about a year of loitering around Sun-Earth L2.

events.label: Earth flyby — Gold
events.description: Gold's powered Earth flyby on 9 November 2026.

events.label: Mars approach
events.description: Blue arrives on 7 September 2027; Gold follows on 9 September.

events.label: Mars orbit insertion
events.description: Orbit-insertion burns of about 11 minutes at 450 km on 7 September (Blue) and 9 September 2027 put the twins into a 60-hour capture orbit; science begins in June 2028.
